Bakes the current film + print look into a 3D LUT. .cube imports into most apps; .clf (Common LUT Format) imports into DaVinci Resolve / OpenColorIO 2.3+. Spatial/stochastic effects (grain, halation, diffusion, glare) can\'t be captured in a 3D LUT and are omitted from the bake.

MALLETT2019 isn\'t implemented yet — both options currently render as HANATOS2025.
Apply the hanatos2025 bandpass adaptation window when reconstructing spectra.
Apply the hanatos2025 surface adaptation polynomial when reconstructing spectra.
Gaussian blur sigma applied to the reconstructed spectra (spectral-axis samples; each sample is 5 nm). 0 = off.
Filter UV light (amplitude, wavelength cutoff nm, sigma nm).

Scale image size up to increase resolution
Crop: enabled (use the crop tool to adjust)
Tap a grey or white area in your photo and the white balance is set to neutralize it. Works on every source — or use the sliders below.
Warm / cool the image. Positive = warmer; 0 = off. Works on every source.
Green ↔ magenta. Positive = magenta, negative = green; 0 = off.

This is a tungsten-balanced stock, so it renders a daylight scene blue — that\'s authentic film behaviour. Turn this on to warm the input to the film\'s reference light and render neutral, like an 85 filter on the lens.
The virtual 85 filter — warms the input to a tungsten stock\'s reference light so it renders neutral. This stock is daylight-balanced (already neutral), so it has no effect here.
RAW camera white balance (re-decodes the file):
Temperature and Tint are used only when \"custom\" is selected above.
Colour temperature in Kelvin for Custom white balance (1000 K – 12000 K).
Green/magenta tint multiplier for Custom white balance (1.0 = neutral).
Replaces isolated stuck or hot photosites with their neighbours before demosaicing. Leaves real highlights alone.
Smooths colour blotches in shadows and high-ISO shots. Brightness and fine detail are kept; only colour is softened.
Add a bias to the auto-exposure of the camera
Long edge of the film format in mm (8, 16, 35, 60, 120)
Sigma of gaussian filter in um for the camera lens blur. Spatial effect — applied only when Halation is enabled (the spatial branch).

Fits a scene wider than the film onto it before exposure: highlights and shadows beyond the knees are compressed smoothly, mid-tones are untouched. Useful for high-contrast phone DNGs. Not part of upstream spektrafilm; idea from SpektraLab.
Stops above the metered mid-grey where highlight compression starts. Below it nothing changes.

How many stops above the knee every highlight is fitted into. Smaller holds more highlight detail but flattens it, and compressed highlights also lose saturation the way they would on the film\'s shoulder; 0 turns highlight compression off. Highlights that were already clipped in the photo have no detail to bring back.
Stops below the metered mid-grey where shadow lifting starts. Above it nothing changes.
How many stops below the knee every shadow is fitted into. Lifting deep shadows also lifts their noise; 0 turns shadow lifting off.
Shape of the roll-off: 1 is the gentlest shoulder, 4 holds the scene closer to linear until near the limit.
Upper bound on how far the deepest shadows are brightened, however far below the knee they sit. Lower keeps blacks black.

Exposes a camera date-back imprint onto the negative, so the LED digits develop, glow and grain with the picture instead of being pasted on top. Not part of upstream spektrafilm; idea from SpektraLab.
How tall the digits are, as a percentage of the picture\'s short edge.
Distance of the imprint from the corner, as a percentage of the picture\'s short edge.
How strongly the LED exposes the film, in stops above mid-grey. Brighter digits bloom more into the picture. Independent of the exposure slider.
Changes the exposure time set in the virtual enlarger
Multigrade filtration on the enlarger: 00 is softest, 5 is hardest. Mid-grey stays put while contrast changes.
Auto adjust the print exposure for the camera exposure compensation ev
Y filter shift from neutral, in Kodak CC units
M filter shift from neutral, in Kodak CC units
Enlarger lens blur is not applicable to the enlarger stage (no engine call site).
Sigma of gaussian filter for the enlarger lens blur
Sigma of gaussian filter in pixel for the scanner lens blur. Spatial effect — applied only when Halation is enabled (the spatial branch).
Scan white/black correction has no effect in Slide mode on a negative stock — it applies only to a slide/positive film, or in print mode. Matches the spektrafilm engine.
Pin the scan\'s white point to the target white level below. Subtle at the default 0.98 — lower the white level to see it pull the highlights down.
Target white level when white correction is enabled
Pin the scan\'s black point to the target black level below. Subtle at the default 0.01 — raise the black level to see it lift the shadows.
Target black level when black correction is enabled
Overall colorfulness of the output. Negative = softer/more muted (tame a too-punchy look); positive = more vivid. Applied after the film render.
Like Saturation but weighted to muted colors, so already-saturated tones (and skin) shift less. Applied after the film render.
ACES-style: softens the harsh cyan/edge fringe on very saturated colors by pulling them toward neutral. 0 = off. Helps when saturated highlights look unnatural.
Add or not the CCTF to the saved image file
Show the scanned film directly instead of a print — the natural view for slide/reversal stocks (a positive). For negative stocks this shows the raw orange negative.
Toggle the diffusion filter on this stage.
Multiplier on the image-plane PSF widths.
Additive offset on the halo warmth axis.
Area of particles in um2, relates to ISO.
Sigma of gaussian blur in pixels for the grain.
Scale of particle area for the RGB layers.
Scale of particle area for the sublayers in each color layer.
Scale the sigma of gaussian blur in um for the dye clouds.
[sigma blur um, molecular clump size nm]
Preflash exposure value in ev for the print
Shift the Y filter from neutral for the preflash (Kodak CC)
Shift the M filter from neutral for the preflash (Kodak CC)
Works on the print route only (no effect in Slide mode / scan-film). Edges and texture keep their contrast, and hard edges get no halo.
How strongly large bright areas are pulled down toward the middle, to bring back sky and highlight detail. 3 is a full mask
How strongly large dark areas are lifted toward the middle, to open up shadow detail. 3 is a full mask
How many stops of print exposure either side of mid-grey the mask leaves completely alone
Blur of the mask as a percentage of the long edge. Smaller follows shapes more tightly; larger is gentler
High-level scatter strength. 1.0 = full physical scatter.
High-level scatter size multiplier (1.0 = physical defaults).
Protected range above midgray for the boost onset in stops.
How quickly the highlight boost ramps in (0-1).
Sigma of the scatter core Gaussian per channel, in um.
Decay constant of the scatter exponential tail per channel, in um.
Weight of the scatter tail Gaussian per channel (0-100%).
Total back-reflection halation amplitude per channel (0-100%).
Sigma of the first halation bounce per channel, in um.
Divide by (1 + sum of bounce amplitudes) so mid-grey is preserved.

Models film\'s chemical color crosstalk (DIR couplers) — the cause of film\'s characteristic color separation and edge effects. Looking for a plain saturation control? Use Saturation / Vibrance in Edit → Color.
Global multiplier on the DIR coupler inhibition matrix.
Cross-layer (off-diagonal) inhibition — how much each dye layer bleeds into the others.
The DIR gamma matrix is set per film stock by the engine (each stock overwrites these) — adjusting them has no effect.
Per-channel same-layer DIR gamma (R, G, B).
Cross-channel DIR inhibition (a color-mixing matrix term): from R onto G and B.
Cross-channel DIR inhibition (a color-mixing matrix term): from G onto R and B.
Cross-channel DIR inhibition (a color-mixing matrix term): from B onto R and G.
Sigma in µm for the diffusion of the couplers (5-20 µm).
Long-range tail sigma in µm for the coupler diffusion.
Weight of the long-range diffusion tail.
Glare applies on the print route only (no effect in Slide mode / scan-film).
Sigma of gaussian blur in pixels for the glare
Gamma factor of the negative density curves.
Gamma factor of the print paper.
Re-develop the print from the paper\'s parametric density-curve model with a coupled-gamma + developer-exhaustion morph. Off = the stock\'s measured curves.
Global coupled gamma applied to all print curves.
Blend toward a Gumbel-matched curve shape (shoulder roll-off); preserves midgray.
Max size of the long edge of the preview image, in pixels.
